sources: Chestnut & Paes, CP Enneagram Academy, 'The Ultimate Guide to the 27 Enneagram Subtypes' (cpenneagram.com/subtypes)
Beatrice Chestnut, 'The Complete Enneagram: 27 Paths to Greater Self-Knowledge' (2013)
Beatrice Chestnut guest blog, The Enneagram in Business (theenneagraminbusiness.com)
Claudio Naranjo, 'Character and Neurosis' / '27 personajes en busca del ser' (via scribd/linktr.ee transcriptions)
Don Riso & Russ Hudson, 'The Wisdom of the Enneagram' (1999); The Enneagram Institute (enneagraminstitute.com)
Personality Database Enneagram wiki; Personality Cafe transcriptions of The Wisdom of the Enneagram [secondary]
_meta.countertype_invariant: exactly one per type; nine total; verified

subtypes.label: Worry (Ichazo: Anxiety)
subtypes.text: Anger is turned inward as anxious over-responsibility; reaction formation converts the heat of anger into warmth, producing the true, benevolent perfectionist who controls the environment to secure survival.
subtypes.school_note: Riso-Hudson: grounded, practical, self-disciplined One; RH give no confirmed one-word title and no 'countertype' concept, treating the instinct as an independent overlay.

subtypes.label: Non-Adaptability (Ichazo: Maladjustment)
subtypes.text: Anger is half-hidden as cool superiority; resentment is channeled into embodying the perfect model of the 'right way,' with a teacher-like, aristocratic rigidity.
subtypes.school_note: Both schools describe a cooler, intellectual One; only Naranjo/Chestnut structure the trio around a countertype.

subtypes.label: Zeal (Ichazo Spanish: celo)
subtypes.text: The only overtly angry One; anger potentiates desire so resentment is redirected outward into a vehement, entitled drive to reform and perfect others. Can resemble an Eight.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut mark SX One as the countertype (anger expressed, not repressed); Riso-Hudson have no equivalent designation.

subtypes.label: Privilege (also Me-First)
subtypes.text: Pride is hardest to detect here; the passion is redirected into a childlike, charming bid to be taken care of, staying youthful and ambivalent about adult connection.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut mark SP Two as the countertype (pride least visible); Riso-Hudson treat SP Two as a domestic/nesting flavor without a countertype label.

subtypes.label: Ambition
subtypes.text: Pride is most visible; the helper's pride is redirected into seducing groups by cultivating an image of influential, super-competent leadership, 'giving to get' with a strategic angle.
subtypes.school_note: Both schools see the Social Two as more powerful/adult; only Naranjo/Chestnut define the trio by contrast to the countertype.

subtypes.label: Seduction/Aggression (Aggressive-Seductive)
subtypes.text: Pride is redirected into classical one-to-one seduction; a 'femme fatale' (or male equivalent) who becomes irresistible to win the single person who will meet all their needs.
subtypes.school_note: Substantial agreement across schools on the seductive one-to-one Two.

subtypes.label: Security
subtypes.text: Self-deception takes the form of a 'vanity for having no vanity'; the Three works to genuinely be good and effective rather than to look good, hiding that image matters at all.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut mark SP Three as the countertype; Riso-Hudson note the Three among the few types with a counter-appearance but reserve 'countertype' to the Naranjo lineage.

subtypes.label: Prestige
subtypes.text: The 'classic' Three; vanity is acted out through visible achievement, status-climbing, and being on stage; the most competitive Three, with a corporate/sales mentality.
subtypes.school_note: Both schools treat this as the prototypical, recognition-seeking Three.

subtypes.label: Charisma (some Naranjo notes: Masculinity/Femininity)
subtypes.text: Vanity is redirected into building a personally attractive image and promoting important others; the most emotional Three, uneasy talking about self, with a team/family mentality.
subtypes.school_note: Naming varies within the Naranjo lineage (Charisma vs. Ichazo's Masculinity/Femininity); Riso-Hudson describe an attractiveness-focused Three.

subtypes.label: Tenacity (Ichazo: Reckless/Dauntless; RH: The Sensualist)
subtypes.text: Envy is redirected away from lament into hard work to acquire what one lacks; long-suffering, stoic, masochistic-not-melodramatic, with a 'passion for effort.'
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut mark SP Four as the countertype; Riso-Hudson title the same combination 'The Sensualist' (focus on comfort/beauty) — same slot, different emphasis.
subtypes.source: cpenneagram.com ('The Countertype'); Chestnut guest blog; Personality Cafe (RH)

subtypes.label: Shame (RH: The Outsider)
subtypes.text: Envy fuels shame, unfavorable comparison, and the victim role; the shyest Four, who finds a paradoxical comfort in melancholy and self-abasement.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo 'Shame'; Riso-Hudson 'The Outsider' for the same combination.

subtypes.label: Competition (Ichazo: Hate; RH: Infatuation)
subtypes.text: Envy becomes competitive anger and 'an envy that wants'; shameless and demanding, this Four externalizes pain and can make others suffer — the angriest Four.
subtypes.school_note: Sharp divergence: Naranjo/Ichazo emphasize rivalry/hate; Riso-Hudson name the same slot 'Infatuation' (romantic obsession).

subtypes.label: Castle (Ichazo: Refuge; Naranjo: Lair; RH: Isolation and Hoarding)
subtypes.text: Avarice is redirected into boundaries — being 'encastled' behind walls with everything needed to survive, minimizing needs to avoid dependence; least expressive Five.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut 'Castle'; Riso-Hudson 'Isolation and Hoarding' for the same combination.

subtypes.label: Totem (RH: The Specialist)
subtypes.text: Avarice is channeled into knowledge and 'super-ideals'; relating to others through shared expertise rather than feeling, hoarding what confers standing, seeking ultimate meaning.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut 'Totem'; Riso-Hudson 'The Specialist' for the same combination.

subtypes.label: Confidence (RH: This Is My World)
subtypes.text: Avarice is redirected into a search for an idealized, wholly trustworthy partner to confide in; the most romantic and emotionally sensitive Five, resembling a Four.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut clearly mark SX Five as the countertype; Riso-Hudson's overlay framing does not designate one. See Part C — a commonly mis-reported countertype.
subtypes.source: cpenneagram.com ('The Countertype'); Chestnut guest blog ('the Five countertype')

subtypes.label: Warmth
subtypes.text: Fear is redirected into seeking warm, trustworthy alliances; the most phobic Six, whose insecurity is managed by friendliness and dependence on protective others.
subtypes.school_note: Both schools describe a warm, alliance-seeking phobic Six.

subtypes.label: Duty (RH secondary: Generating Support)
subtypes.text: Fear is managed by adherence to rules, reason, and authority; the 'Prussian'/lawgiver Six who becomes over-sure as a defense against uncertainty, disliking ambiguity.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut 'Duty'; a Riso-Hudson secondary title 'Generating Support' is reported (Truity).

subtypes.label: Strength/Beauty
subtypes.text: The counterphobic Six goes against fear by becoming strong and intimidating ('the best defense is a good offense'); per Chestnut quoting Naranjo, Ichazo's title meant strength in men, beauty in women.
subtypes.school_note: The point of nearest agreement: both schools treat the counterphobic Sexual Six as the well-known counter-appearance; only Naranjo/Chestnut formalize 'countertype.'

subtypes.label: Keepers of the Castle (Naranjo: Family; Ichazo: Defenders; RH: Getting Mine)
subtypes.text: Gluttony (experiential hunger) is redirected into building a partisan 'good mafia' network of allies and family; pragmatic, opportunistic, alert to any advantage.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo 'Family'/'Keepers of the Castle'; Riso-Hudson 'Getting Mine' for the same combination.

subtypes.label: Sacrifice
subtypes.text: 'Counter-gluttony': the Seven sacrifices its own desires to serve others and ideals, becoming ascetic and wanting to be seen as good/pure — gluttony inverted into idealistic self-denial.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut mark SO Seven as the countertype; Riso-Hudson agree it is the atypical Seven but do not use the term.

subtypes.label: Suggestibility (also Fascination; RH: The Neophile)
subtypes.text: Gluttony for a higher, idealized world; a dreamer viewing reality through rose-colored, in-love optimism, susceptible to enthusiasm and fantasy.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo 'Suggestibility'; Riso-Hudson 'The Neophile' for the same combination.

subtypes.label: Satisfaction (Ichazo: Satisfactory Survival; RH: The Survivor)
subtypes.text: Lust (intensity/excess) is focused on timely satisfaction of material needs and low tolerance for frustration; the least expressive, most armed and self-sufficient Eight.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo 'Satisfaction'; Riso-Hudson 'The Survivor' for the same combination.

subtypes.label: Solidarity (Ichazo: Friendship; Naranjo: Complicity; RH: Gusto and Camaraderie)
subtypes.text: A 'social antisocial' Eight; lust and aggression are redirected into protecting and standing with others, appearing less aggressive and more loyal than the other Eights.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut mark SO Eight as the countertype; Riso-Hudson label the same combination 'Gusto and Camaraderie.'

subtypes.label: Possession (RH: Taking Charge)
subtypes.text: Lust becomes rebellion and a need to possess everyone's attention — an energetic takeover of the whole scene, seeking power over people and things rather than material security.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo 'Possession'; Riso-Hudson 'Taking Charge' for the same combination.

subtypes.label: Appetite
subtypes.text: Sloth (self-forgetting) is expressed by merging with physical comforts and routines — eating, sleeping, familiar absorbing activities — substituting these for contact with one's own being; most solitary Nine.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut 'Appetite'; Riso-Hudson describe a comfort-seeking, routine-bound Nine.

subtypes.label: Participation
subtypes.text: Self-forgetting is redirected into fusing with groups and working hard — even to workaholism — to belong; the high activity level runs against the type's usual inertia.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut mark SO Nine as the countertype; Riso-Hudson agree it is the atypically active Nine but do not use the term.

subtypes.label: Fusion (also Union)
subtypes.text: Sloth is expressed by merging with one important other, unconsciously taking on their attitudes, opinions and feelings because standing alone feels too hard; gentle and unassertive.
subtypes.school_note: Naranjo/Chestnut 'Fusion'/'Union'; Riso-Hudson describe a merging, self-losing Nine in one-to-one bonds.
